text: Read the meanings of the names from Adam to Noah: "Man is appointed mortal sorrow, but the blessed God shall come down, teaching. His death shall bring the despairing rest."
explanation:
Genesis 5 looks like a dull list of who lived how long. But take the names in order and look up their commonly given meanings: Adam, man; Seth, appointed; Enosh, mortal; Kenan, sorrow; Mahalalel, the blessed God; Jared, shall come down; Enoch, teaching; Methuselah, his death shall bring; Lamech, often linked with despair or power; Noah, rest.

Read together, they tell the gospel in the very first pages of Scripture, long before the cross. God hides treasure even in names. Ask Him to open your eyes, and dull chapters can light up with Jesus.

text: Methuselah's name has been read as "when he dies, it will come." He lived 969 years, longer than anyone in Scripture.
explanation:
Enoch walked with God after his son Methuselah was born, as if the name itself were a prophecy, pointing to the judgment of the flood. Imagine the household holding its breath every time the boy fell sick. And yet God let him live longer than any other man on record.

The flood came in the year Methuselah died. God must execute justice, or evil runs unchecked. But His heart is love, and He waited and waited. "The Lord is not slack concerning His promise… but is longsuffering toward us, not willing that any should perish." He's still that patient today.

text: The word in prayer was "creative miracles": what's worn out, removed or missing, God can make new.
explanation:
Praying the night before the service, Joseph Prince kept hearing two words: creative miracles. Not just healing of what's sick, but recreation of what's gone: an organ that's been removed, a spine that's degenerated, a mind that's growing foggy. Doctors do their best with natural means, and we thank God for them.

But Jesus said, "With men it is impossible, but not with God; for with God all things are possible." If you've received a hard report, don't accept it as the final word. Ask Him for a creative miracle, then step out and do what you couldn't do before.

text: "Do not be afraid; only believe." Before Jesus healed, He often dealt with fear first.
explanation:
Messengers came to Jairus with the worst news a father could hear: "Your daughter is dead. Why trouble the Teacher any further?" Jesus overheard and immediately said, "Do not be afraid; only believe." Then He went in and raised her.

If you've just had a bad report from the doctor, hear Him say the same to you. Fear shrinks your expectation; faith opens the door. People of the world look ahead as they age and see only decline. You have a different future. He wants you well now, and eternal life awaits you.

text: Revelation foretold an event in Jerusalem that the whole world would watch. For centuries that seemed impossible.
explanation:
When John wrote it, Jerusalem was about to be destroyed, and for nearly two thousand years it lay largely desolate; Mark Twain described the land as barren and forsaken. Scripture said the people of every nation would see something happen there. Who could imagine the world watching one street in one city? And who would rebuild Jerusalem?

The Jews returned and Israel was reborn in 1948, and today live broadcasts reach every nation in an instant. Scripture describes wars and rumours of wars, plagues and great earthquakes increasing in the last days. Don't be afraid like those without hope. The Word you hold is more advanced than any headline.

text: Being male is a matter of birth. Being a man is a matter of choice.
explanation:
In a culture that blurs God's design, go back to the original: "Male and female He created them." God wasn't confused. To the men: don't let anyone shame you out of your masculinity. Take responsibility. Protect your wife and children. If you're afraid, do it afraid. And if your wife needs to win the argument, let her; that's part of being a man too.

Teach your sons, as they grow, to honour and care for women. And a woman's femininity flourishes most when her man is allowed to be a man. "Watch, stand fast in the faith, be brave, be strong."

text: Bees kept getting into his toddler's room. He drew a line in Jesus' name, and the next morning dead bees lay along it.
explanation:
In a rented home, bees came in through the balcony at night, and his little daughter would wake up hearing them buzz. Joseph Prince walked the room, anointed the windows with oil, and declared a bloodline of Jesus across her bed area. The next day the family found dead bees along the line. They hadn't crossed.

"When I see the blood, I will pass over you." The blood of Jesus isn't a vague religious idea; it's what covers you and your family. Every time he boards a plane, he quietly lays his hand on it and covers it with the blood. Don't take your safety for granted. Plead the blood over what God has given you.
